findings.statement: A smaller index makes a bulk load faster
findings.detail: varint index 1145201 ops/s against flat 816259 (varint vs flat: greater 1.403x (p=0.0022, rel_iqr 7.6%/13.0%)), with the file at 105.5 MB against 168.6 and the checkpoint at 0.342s against 0.663s, of which fsync is 0.132s against 0.233s. This is f31's flush half tested directly: if the bytes the index adds are what the checkpoint is paying for, removing 73.5% of them has to show here

findings.statement: The flat index reads faster than the varint one it replaced
findings.detail: flat 1884035 reads/s against varint 1906483 (flat vs varint: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 0.988, p=0.6365) -- within noise, not a result). This is the side a smaller index costs, and it is why F11.4 accepts +73.5% on the file deliberately: a section read in place cannot be compressed, and a compressed one is copied into every reader's heap

notes: both arms interleaved; the only difference is Options::flat_index
keys arrive in order, the shape EXT.13 finds Supdb behind on
